Choosing 10 picks is pretty hard. Sometimes there is a clear contender for a pick, someone who looks like they could be pushing daisies by March, but I find keeping a balanced pick list is the best way to maximise points.

Let's say, for example, you've picked 10 celebrities in their nineties who are looking pretty frail. That's great - those are some guaranteed points - but you also need to take some chances if you want your name to be at the top of the leaderboard on New Year's Day. To do this, you're going to have to pick someone young enough to score big points. One of the best things you can do is research celebrities with terminal illnesses, as they are almost definitely going to die within the next few years. Pancreatic cancer is your friend.

My advice to anyone wishing to shoot for the big points is this:

* 6 likely to guaranteed picks. This will be the base of death that you build from. Your morbid point generator. Getting points on the board is essential, you don't want to miss out on the First Blood bonus.

* 2-3 medium picks. These picks are slightly less likely to happen, but yield more points. When these picks die, you won't be unsurprised, and will probably ask how they came to perish. In my opinion, these are the most important picks. If you can get 2 of these picks correct, you will be in the top 3 without a doubt.

* The Wildcard. This pick comes up very rarely. It can be a game changer. November is almost up, and you're only halfway up the leaderboard. Prince Philip died in May, and you almost scored big when Charlie Sheen had a botched suicide attempt, but then BANG. You turn on the TV and Kim Jong Un has been assassinated.

Remember that the key to winning is not by choosing the easy picks.
